newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Russia successfully launches Inmarsat satellite.
newsitem.headline: Russia successfully launches Inmarsat satellite.

text.p: Russia successfully launched a U.S.-built satellite for the international telecommunications organisation Inmarsat on Friday.
The Inmarsat-3 satellite was blasted into space on a four-stage Proton rocket from Russia's Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
Interfax news agency said the 1,130 kg satellite was built by U.S. firm Astro Space, part of Lockheed Martin, and cost $80 million.

The launch was the second of 20 commercial satellite launches planned by the year 2000 under an agreement between Russia's Khrunichev Space Centre and the U.S.-backed joint venture International Launch Services (ILS).
In April, the ILS launched the U.S.-built Astra-1F telecommunications satellite ordered by the Societe Europeenne des Satellites (SES). It was also put into orbit by a Proton.
Friday's launch was another step in growing space cooperation between the two former Cold War enemies.
It includes a $190-million deal signed by Khrunichev and Boeing Co. in 1995 to develop and launch the first module of the Alpha international space station.
